title: The Quran: English Meanings and Notes
author: Saheeh International (translation committee)
publication_date: 1997 (first published); most commonly referred to editions are from 2004 and 2011
target_audience: English-speaking Muslims seeking accessible yet precise translation
Non-Muslims interested in understanding the Islamic scripture
Students of religion, theology, and comparative studies
Anyone seeking a clear, linguistic translation of the Quran
core_themes: Monotheism and the oneness of God
Prophethood and the teachings of previous prophets
primary_purpose: To present a clear, accurate, and comprehensible English translation of the original Arabic Quran accompanied by brief explanatory notes, thereby making the core messages and teachings of Islam accessible to English-speaking audiences.

structure_format.narrative_style: Formal, neutral, and literal translation with modern English usage
structure_format.organization: 114 chapters (Surahs) arranged in traditional order; verses (Ayat) are numbered and sometimes grouped by theme in notes
features: Side-by-side Arabic and English text in some editions
Concise explanatory notes to clarify historical, linguistic, and theological points
Footnotes and cross-referencing for ease of study

key_concepts_lessons: God is one, merciful, and the ultimate creator of all things.
Mankind is responsible for following God’s revealed guidance and moral law.
Prophets were sent to all peoples for their guidance, culminating with Muhammad.
Social justice, charity, and compassion are mandated alongside personal piety.
Belief in the afterlife, accountability, and the ultimate justice of God motivates ethical living.
Revelation includes principles for personal character, community, family, law, and worship.
Faith, patience, and perseverance are praised and rewarded.
style_tone: Respectful, measured, and faithful to Arabic meaning
Concise and unembellished explanatory notes for clarity
notable_features: Emphasis on linguistic accuracy and readability for modern audiences
Brief but effective notes bridge cultural and historical contexts
Widespread use in Islamic educational settings and as personal reference
Collaborative translation by a team of three female scholars
cultural_historical_context: Saheeh International's translation emerged in the 1990s-2000s, during a global increase in demand for accessible and reliable English renditions of the Quran, particularly from younger generations and those seeking a modern idiomatic translation without interpretative bias.
reception_impact: Highly regarded among English-speaking Muslim communities for clarity, faithfulness, and simplicity
Endorsed by many contemporary scholars and Islamic institutions
Critically praised for avoiding archaic or difficult language
Some users note the notes are brief and may require supplemental study for in-depth discussion
comparable_titles: The Qur’an: English Translation and Parallel Arabic Text by M.A.S. Abdel Haleem
The Glorious Qur’an (Translation and Commentary) by Abdullah Yusuf Ali
